artifact: CompCert verified C compiler (Coq proof of semantic preservation for the compilation passes); tested version CompCert 1.6 for PowerPC. Paper: Yang, Chen, Eide, Regehr, 'Finding and Understanding Bugs in C Compilers', PLDI 2011, https://users.cs.utah.edu/~regehr/papers/pldi11-preprint.pdf
property: Semantic preservation: generated assembly behaves as the CompCert C source semantics prescribe (for the verified passes).
model: CompCert's formal semantics of its C subset and of the target assembly (PowerPC); proof covers the pass chain between those formal languages.
trusted_base: unverified front-end (parsing, elaboration of C into CompCert's input language)
formal semantics of C subset and of PowerPC assembly
assumptions: the input program is translated correctly into the verified source language
the PPC assembly semantics matches what the real assembler accepts (e.g. immediate width limits)
deployed: CompCert 1.6 binary run on Csmith-generated programs, emitting PowerPC code.
gap: Csmith found silent wrong-code bugs in CompCert 1.6, all in parts outside the proof: the unverified front-end (integer promotion/implicit casts) and a PPC semantics that omitted the 16-bit displacement constraint, deferring to the assembler; no wrong-code bugs were found in the verified middle-end.
